name: terrain is drawn a canvas at a time, in both screens that draw a map

steps.note: huge is 256x256 = 65,536 cells. Entering used to spawn a sprite for every
one of them in a single OnEnter; the canvas shows about eighty.

steps.shot: the editor, a canvas of a 256x256 map

steps.note: painting still writes the map first and draws from it second, which is what
keeps the screen from showing a tile no saved file contains

steps.shot: a wall painted in the middle of a huge map

steps.note: and it is in the saved file, not merely on screen
the same map in the game screen, from the same palette and the same window
panning a long way re-points the same sprites rather than accumulating them:
if the window leaked one per cell crossed, this would be hundreds by now

steps.shot: somewhere else on the same huge map

steps.note: zooming out grows the canvas, so the window grows with it and stays bounded

steps.shot: zoomed out on a huge map

steps.note: leaving and coming straight back: the sprites went with DespawnOnExit, so a
window still holding them would re-point entities that no longer exist and
draw an empty map - which every ceiling in this file would happily accept

steps.shot: the same map, entered a second time
